name.en-US: foxvoice — push to talk for your browser

summary.en-US: Hold a button, speak, and hear the answer. Speech to text runs in your browser with Whisper, and the reply is spoken with a voice on your computer. Audio and text stay on your computer.

description.en-US:
foxvoice adds push to talk to the sidebar. Hold the button, or hold Space on it, while you speak. Let go, and the sidebar shows what you said, gets a reply from a model on your computer, and reads the reply aloud.

**Who it is for:** people who want to talk to an AI model or agent on their own computer, with no cloud speech service.

**What it does**

- Turns the microphone on only while you hold the button. It turns it off when you let go.
- Turns speech into text with Whisper tiny.en in the browser (English).
- Shows how sure the model is of what it heard, and asks you again when it is not sure.
- Asks a model server on your computer for a reply, for example llama-server or Ollama.
- Reads the reply aloud with a voice of your operating system.

**What leaves your computer, and when**

- Nothing, in normal use. Audio and text go only to the speech model in the browser, and to servers on this computer (127.0.0.1) when you choose them in Settings.
- The speech model downloads from Hugging Face once (43 MB). These requests hold no audio and no text.
- foxvoice has no server and sends nothing to its authors.

**Permissions**

- Access to 127.0.0.1: talk to whisper-server and to the model server on your computer.
- Storage and unlimited storage: settings and the speech model files stay in your browser.
- The microphone: Firefox asks you the first time. The setup page asks in a tab if the sidebar cannot.

foxvoice is an early version. The source code is MIT licensed.

version.approval_notes: The uploaded source.zip is the git tree of this release. To build: install Node 24 and pnpm 11 (corepack enable), run `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, then `pnpm build:ext`. The output is dist-ext/. esbuild bundles extension/*.js with src/, foxmind and transformers.js; transformers.js is its own chunk in vendor/. ort/ holds ONNX Runtime's WASM files from the npm package onnxruntime-web, unmodified. To try it: click the toolbar button to open the sidebar, hold the button and speak. The first use downloads the Whisper model from Hugging Face. Replies need a model server on 127.0.0.1 (llama-server on port 8080); without one, the reply says so. No account is needed.

http://127.0.0.1/*.host_permission: The add-on sends the user's speech to whisper-server and the transcript to a model server that the user runs on this computer, so the audio and text stay local.
